touches.text: Code that is no longer needed is deleted. Git history keeps it if we ever need it back.
A device's code lives in cairn/devices/<device>/; its data in ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/.
The exceptions are client tools a device publishes:
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.

A tooth whose live subject was deleted retires with it, when fixture teeth still cover the behaviour. Akien 2026-11-12, answering Q#87 (ce92eb562cf9 clause 6 read 6890cf7e4053's clause-2 tooth, deleted with the inference_calls table by 98ab0e9db57f): "i am good with retiring that".
Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Akien 2026-11-13: "every test failure, every orphaned file, HAS TO BE FIXED. if we get 3 reds but they're really not related to what we just did, we can ticket them for fixing. reds don't get lost." and "so each run writes any new bugs". Once a red unrelated to a crossing is ticketed, that crossing can go ahead.

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, "because even the basic laws rest finally upon those core principles" (Akien 2026-11-13). Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).
TOOLS: base, validation_store, proof_coverage, scratch, question, proof_discovery, chain, bus_client, artifact, system_word; machine build_inspector; db client.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. Akien 2026-11-09 (Q#77): "wouldn't it be easier (for the python code anyway) to see if the imports do not include other device paths?"
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
